title: Multiplying 3- to 4-Digit by 1-Digit and 2- to 3-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Multiplication Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Multiply two numbers with and without regrouping: 3- to 4-digit numbers by a 1-digit number, and 2- to 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers, with products up to 1 000 000; estimate the result of multiplying two numbers where the product is less than 1 000 000.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 multiplication worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: multiply by 1-digit and 2-digit numbers, area models and estimating products. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Find partial products, then add them.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Multiply the ones first, then the tens, hundreds and so on. Add any regrouped digit.
  • For a 2-digit multiplier, find two partial products: one for the ones digit and one for the tens digit (start that row with a 0).
  • Add the partial products.
  • Estimate by rounding each factor: 387 × 42 is about 400 × 40 = 16,000.

Examples

Example

236 × 47

236 × 7 = 1,652

236 × 40 = 9,440

1,652 + 9,440

Answer: 11,092

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the regrouped digitAdd it after you multiply the next place.
No zero in the second rowThe tens digit makes tens: start with 0.
Adding partial products wrongLine up the places.

items.q: Round 3,746 to the nearest thousand to estimate 3,746 × 4.
items.e: 3,746 has 7 hundreds, so it rounds up to 4,000. 4,000 × 4 = 16,000. The exact answer is 14,984.

items.q: Round 6,281 to the nearest thousand to estimate 6,281 × 3.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate 67 × 48.
items.e: 67 rounds up to 70 and 48 rounds up to 50. 70 × 50 = 3,500. The exact answer is 3,216, close to the estimate.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate 83 × 26.

items.q: The school canteen sells 312 plates of fried rice each week. About how many plates does it sell in 8 weeks?
items.e: Round 312 to the nearest hundred: 300. 300 × 8 = 2,400. Do not round 8 to 10: that gives 3,000, which is too far off. The exact answer is 312 × 8 = 2,496.

items.q: A theatre sells 1,985 tickets for each show. About how many tickets does it sell for 4 shows?
items.e: Round 1,985 to the nearest thousand: 2,000. 2,000 × 4 = 8,000. (Rounding 1,985 down to 1,000 gives 4,000, far too small.) The exact answer is 1,985 × 4 = 7,940.

items.q: A stadium has 48 rows with 215 seats in each row. About how many seats are there?
items.e: Round 215 to 200 and 48 to 50. 200 × 50 = 10,000. (Rounding 48 down to 40 gives 8,000.) The exact answer is 215 × 48 = 10,320.

items.q: Liza reads 28 pages of a storybook each day. About how many pages does she read in 31 days?
items.e: Round 28 to 30 and 31 to 30. 30 × 30 = 900. (Using 20 × 30 = 600 rounds 28 the wrong way.) The exact answer is 28 × 31 = 868.

items.e: Estimate: 72 × 39 is about 70 × 40 = 2,800. 2,808 is close to 2,800, so the answer is reasonable.
